About Company:
Afghan Health and Development Services (AHDS) is a not-for-profit, non-governmental, and non-political organization founded by Afghans on April 7th, 1990.  AHDS is an active member of the Afghan NGOs Coordination Bureau (ANCB), the Agency Coordinating Body for Afghan Relief (ACBAR), and the Alliance of Health Organizations (AHO). Job Summary:
Background:
Midwives working in Family Health Houses (FHHs) play a critical role in providing essential maternal, newborn and related health services to women and girls in Afghanistan. Their work can involve prolonged exposure to demanding working conditions, high workloads, emotional stress, challenging cases and other pressures that may affect their psychosocial well-being. Recognizing the importance of staff welfare and the well-being of frontline health workers, it is critical to engage a qualified and experienced MHPSS Senior Counsellor to provide accessible, confidential and professional psychosocial support to midwives working in selected FHHs. The intervention will focus on the identified FHHs in Helmand and Kandahar.
Key Responsibilities:
The MHPSS Senior Counsellor will be responsible for the following:
1. Psychosocial Counselling and Support
●
Conduct in-person psychosocial counselling and supportive sessions with midwives working in the targeted FHHs.
●
Provide individual counselling, psychological first aid and psychosocial support based on identified needs.
●
Establish a safe, confidential, respectful and non-judgmental environment for midwives to discuss work-related stress, emotional difficulties, interpersonal concerns and other psychosocial issues.
●
Apply appropriate evidence-informed counselling and psychosocial support approaches within the counsellor's professional scope of practice.
●
Support midwives to develop healthy coping strategies, strengthen resilience and maintain their psychosocial well-being.
2. Assessment and Follow-up
●
Conduct an initial assessment of the psychosocial well-being and support needs of individual midwives.
●
Develop, jointly with each midwife, an appropriate follow-up and communication plan based on identified needs.
●
Provide follow-up counselling and psychosocial support through telephone or in-person, as appropriate.
●
Maintain regular and appropriate contact with midwives requiring continued psychosocial support.
●
Monitor progress and adjust the frequency and type of support according to individual needs.
3. Referral and Case Management
●
Identify individuals who may require specialized mental health, or other professional services beyond the scope of the counselling provided.
●
Facilitate appropriate and confidential referrals to available specialized services in accordance with established referral pathways.
●
Follow up on referrals, where appropriate and with the individual's consent, while respecting confidentiality and professional boundaries.
●
Document referrals and follow-up actions in a confidential and anonymized manner, as required.
●
Follow up the action plans and work to solve it accordingly.
4. Staff Welfare and Capacity Support
●
Contribute to the overall staff welfare approach for midwives working in targeted facilities.
●
Identify common psychosocial stressors and emerging staff welfare concerns affecting midwives.
●
Where appropriate, provide brief group-based psychosocial support, stress-management or well-being sessions for midwives.
●
Provide practical recommendations on measures that may contribute to improved staff well-being and retention.
●
Support the development of simple, context-appropriate staff welfare and self-care tools or guidance materials for midwives, where feasible.
●
5. Coordination and Reporting
●
Coordinate closely with the supervisor and designated focal point of the implementing partner.
●
Maintain appropriate documentation of counselling and psychosocial support activities while ensuring strict confidentiality.
●
Provide regular anonymized reports on counselling activities, psychosocial needs, key challenges, referrals, and recommendations to strengthen staff welfare and support.
●
Immediately communicate any significant operational or service-delivery concerns through the appropriate reporting channels, while maintaining client confidentiality.
●
Participate in relevant coordination, review and planning meetings as requested.
●
Ensure that all MHPSS activities are implemented in line with relevant national and international ethical guidelines, including do-no-harm, informed consent and confidentiality principles.
●
Approach and Modality:
The assignment will follow a blended model of MHPSS support, combining face-to-face and remote counselling. The MHPSS Senior Counsellor will initially visit the targeted FHHs and MLMCCs to establish contact with midwives, conduct an initial psychosocial assessment and provide counselling/support. Following the initial visit, the counsellor will develop an individualized follow-up plan with each midwife. Subsequent support may be provided through telephone-based counselling and psychosocial check-ins, particularly for midwives working in remote locations. The frequency of follow-up will be determined according to the individual midwife's needs and the agreed communication plan. The MHPSS counsellor is expected to ensure that the modality of support is accessible, confidential, culturally appropriate and consistent with professional ethical standards.
Reporting and Supervision:
The MHPSS Senior Counsellor will work under the overall supervision of the designated IP Project Manager.
Job Requirements:
Required Qualifications and Experience:
Education
●
A Master's degree in Psychology (2 years psychological special training and certificate) , Counselling, Clinical Psychology, Mental Health, Social Work or another relevant field is required/preferred, depending on the applicable recruitment requirements.
Professional Experience and Technical Competencies
●
Minimum 4 years of relevant professional experience in MHPSS, psychosocial counselling, mental health or related programming.
●
Demonstrated experience providing individual psychosocial counselling and support.
●
Experience working with health workers, frontline workers or other personnel exposed to high-stress or demanding working environments is highly desirable.
●
Experience in staff welfare, psychological first aid, stress management, resilience-building or related interventions is an advantage.
●

●
Ability to work independently, manage a caseload and organize field visits and remote follow-up effectively.
●
Experience working in Afghanistan or similar conflict-affected or humanitarian contexts is highly desirable.
●

●

About Company:
Aga Khan Health Services (AKHS) is one of the most comprehensive private, not‐for‐profit health care systems in the developing world with community health programs in large geographical areas in Central and South Asia, as well as in East Africa.
The Aga Khan Health Services, Afghanistan (AKHS, A) was established in 2003 as part of the Aga Khan Development Network (AKDN). AKHS, A provides health care services mainly on behalf of the government including the Ministry of Public Health’s of Afghanistan’s Basic Package of Health Services (BPHS) and Essential Package of Hospital Services (EPHS). AKHS, A is unique both in scale and scope, delivering critical health services along the continuum of care, from Community Health Workers (CHWs) to ISO certified hospital facilities.
AKHS, A is currently implementing healthcare services in Bamyan, Baghlan, Badakhshan, Kabul and Takhar provinces. The agency’s scope of work includes the provision of primary and secondary healthcare, preventive and curative medical care, Nursing and Midwifery education, Human Resources Development and Hospital Management. As BPHS and EPHS implementer, AKHS, A provides technical support as well as capacity building of health personnel, immunization services, nutrition trainings and the training of Community Health Nurses and Community Health Midwives.
AKHS, A draws on internal and other donor fundings to continue supplementary and complementary support to the national health system. Moreover, AKHS, A has introduced innovations, including, expansions of e-Health services, e-learning initiatives, and cross border arrangements. To promote healthy environment, AKHS, A is also implementing net zero and greenhouse gas emission initiatives.

Job Summary:
The
Courier Officer
is responsible for the efficient, safe, and timely coordination, handling, documentation, tracking, and delivery of documents, parcels, and cargo shipments through airlines, airports, courier services, and other transportation channels.
The position coordinates with customers, airlines, customs authorities, airport personnel, government authorities, courier companies, and other relevant stakeholders to ensure that shipments are properly processed, documented, dispatched, tracked, and delivered in accordance with

policies, airline requirements, airport procedures, customs requirements, and applicable regulations.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
A. Cargo & Courier Operations
Coordinate the collection, acceptance, handling, dispatch, transportation, and delivery of shipments.
Determine appropriate transportation methods and routes based on destination, shipment type, urgency, weight, dimensions, and customer requirements.
Coordinate multiple shipments for different customers simultaneously.
Ensure shipments are processed and dispatched within agreed timelines.
Verify shipment details before acceptance and dispatch.
Ensure proper handling and safeguarding of all customer shipments.
Coordinate transportation of shipments to and from the airport when required.
Report any loss, damage, discrepancy, or irregularity immediately to the supervisor.
B. Shipment Documentation
Prepare, verify, and maintain Air Waybills (AWBs), invoices, receipts, shipment forms, and other required documents.
Verify consignor and consignee information.
Record shipment quantity, weight, dimensions, origin, destination, date, time, and tracking/reference number.
Ensure all required documents are complete and accurate before shipment dispatch.
Maintain organized physical and electronic shipment records.
Immediately report missing or incorrect documentation to the responsible supervisor.
C. Airline & Airport Coordination
Coordinate with airline cargo departments and representatives regarding shipment acceptance, booking, loading, transit, arrival, and delivery.
Coordinate with airport authorities and relevant personnel regarding cargo and courier operations.
Follow up on airline schedules, shipment status, delays, and operational issues.
Ensure shipments comply with airline and airport handling procedures.
Coordinate shipment handover to authorized airline or airport personnel.
E. Shipment Tracking & Follow-Up
Track shipments from acceptance through final delivery.
Monitor shipment status and expected delivery times.
Follow up on delayed, missing, damaged, or misrouted shipments.
Coordinate with airlines, courier companies, and other service providers to resolve shipment problems.
Provide timely updates to customers and management.
Maintain records of shipment exceptions, delays, complaints, and corrective actions.
F.
Computer & Reporting
Enter and maintain shipment information in company systems and databases.
Use shipment tracking and barcode systems where applicable.
Use online airline and courier tracking systems.
Maintain shipment records using Microsoft Excel and other Microsoft Office applications.
Prepare daily, weekly, or monthly shipment reports as required.
Maintain confidentiality of customer, shipment, financial, and company information.

Accuracy and completeness of shipment documentation.
Accuracy of shipment records and tracking information.
Reduction of shipment delays and documentation errors.

Proper communication with customers and external stakeholders.

Title: Vaccinator

About Company:
Over the past few years, Afghanistan has witnessed a relative improvement in security and stability across much of the country. This has allowed humanitarian actors like INTERSOS to maintain uninterrupted access and expand services in areas that were previously hard to reach. Despite this progress, the humanitarian situation remains critical, with millions of Afghans continuing to face acute vulnerabilities due to prolonged economic hardship, natural disasters, and limited access to essential services.
In 2025, more than half of the population is in need of humanitarian assistance, with food insecurity, child malnutrition, and displacement remaining key concerns. Natural disasters, such as floods and recent earthquakes, have further compounded the needs of already struggling communities.
INTERSOS continues to operate through a community-based approach with field bases in Kabul, Kandahar, and Zabul, delivering primary healthcare, nutrition, and protection services with a focus on women, children, and persons with disabilities. The organization enjoys strong community acceptance and collaborates closely with relevant national authorities, including maintaining the full participation of female staff in all activities.
While the operational environment is largely stable and conducive, funding shortfalls and systemic barriers such as restrictions on financial flows and administrative bottlenecks continue to impact the scope and scale of humanitarian response. Sustained support is crucial to ensure the continuity of life-saving services and to address the urgent needs of Afghanistan’s most vulnerable populations.
Job Summary:
Contribute to the reduction of mortality and morbidity in the target area, in particular from vaccine-preventable diseases, by delivering routine immunisation services to children and to women of childbearing age, in accordance with the national EPI guidelines, the WHO and UNICEF protocols and the INTERSOS procedures.
The Vaccinator administers vaccines, maintains the cold chain, keeps accurate immunisation records, raises community awareness and follows up defaulters, working in the health facility and with the Mobile Health Team.
2.
Tasks and responsibilities
Delivery of immunisation services
•
Carry out the EPI activities of the project, in the fixed centre and through outreach and mobile health team activities.
•
Administer only the vaccines for which he/she has been trained and assessed as competent, and only after the competency assessment has been recorded by the EPI Officer.
•
Screen every child and every woman of childbearing age against the immunisation schedule, check the vaccination card, and administer the doses due.
•
Apply injection safety at all times: one sterile syringe and needle for each injection, no recapping, and immediate disposal in the safety box.
•
Explain to the caregiver what has been given, the possible minor reactions, and the date of the next dose, and record it on the vaccination card.
•
Never request or accept any payment for vaccination. The service is free of charge.
Cold chain and vaccine management
•
Transport and store vaccines in accordance with the EPI, UNICEF and WHO protocols.
•
Respect the cold chain principles during the transport of vaccines at all times.
•
Check the vaccine vial monitor and the expiry date before administering any dose, and discard any vaccine that does not comply, in accordance with the protocol.
•
Record the temperature of the cold chain equipment as required, and keep the record available for supervision.
•
Where a problem arises in the storage of vaccines, act immediately to transfer them to another location where a functioning cold chain is available, and inform the supervisor without delay.
•
Monitor stock levels and expiry dates, limit wastage, and alert the supervisor in advance of any risk of rupture.
Safety and adverse events
•
Recognise and manage adverse events following immunisation in accordance with the national protocol, ensure that the anaphylaxis kit is available and within its expiry date before any session begins, and keep the patient under observation as required.
•
Report every adverse event following immunisation to the EPI Officer and to the Medical Doctor without delay, and record it.
•
Apply infection prevention and control and the correct management of immunisation waste, including sharps, both in the health facility and in the mobile health team.
Community awareness, coverage and defaulter tracing
•
Raise awareness in the community and encourage caregivers to vaccinate their children and women of childbearing age.
•
Contribute to the extension of vaccination coverage in the catchment area and to the reduction of the defaulter rate.
•
Follow up the completed cases to confirm that the vaccination schedule has been completed, and identify and trace defaulting and missed children together with the Community Health Workers.
•
Participate in new EPI programmes and in public awareness campaigns.
Planning, records and reporting
•
Contribute to the preparation of an accurate working plan for the field activities of the Mobile Health Team.
•
Complete the tally sheets, registers and vaccination cards accurately and on the same day. No eligible child or woman is left unregistered, and no figure is adjusted in order to influence a reported indicator.
•
Know and work towards the annual and monthly EPI indicators of the project.
•
Report to the supervisor any problem encountered in the delivery of services, and any error or near miss occurring in the field activities of the mobile team.
Conduct and compliance
•
Treat every caregiver, child and community member with respect and without discrimination.
•
Maintain the confidentiality of the information recorded in the course of the activity.
•
Comply with the INTERSOS Charter of Values, Code of Ethics, the Policy for the Protection from Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), the Safeguarding Policy and the Anti-Fraud Policy, and report any concern through the established channels.
•
Perform any other task related to the function of the position, as assigned by the supervisor.

Job Summary:
Midwives working in Family Health Houses (FHHs) and Midwifery-Led Maternity Care Centres (MLMCCs) play a critical role in providing essential maternal, newborn and related health services to women and girls in Afghanistan. Their work can involve prolonged exposure to demanding working conditions, high workloads, emotional stress, challenging cases, and other pressures that may affect their psychosocial well-being. Recognizing the importance of staff welfare and the well-being of frontline health workers, it is critical to engage a qualified and experienced MHPSS Senior Counsellor to provide accessible, confidential, and professional psychosocial support to midwives working in selected FHHs and MLMCCs. The intervention will focus on the identified FHHs in Balkh and MLMCCs in Kabul and Logar.
Responsibilities and scope of work:
The MHPSS Senior Counsellor will be responsible for the following:
1. Psychosocial Counselling and Support
●
Conduct in-person psychosocial counselling and supportive sessions with midwives working in the targeted FHHs and MLMCCs.
●
Provide individual counselling, psychological first aid and psychosocial support based on identified needs.
●
Establish a safe, confidential, respectful and non-judgmental environment for midwives to discuss work-related stress, emotional difficulties, interpersonal concerns and other psychosocial issues.
●
Apply appropriate evidence-informed counselling and psychosocial support approaches within the counsellor's professional scope of practice.
●
Support midwives to develop healthy coping strategies, strengthen resilience and maintain their psychosocial well-being.
2. Assessment and Follow-up
●
Conduct an initial assessment of the psychosocial well-being and support needs of individual midwives.
●
Develop, jointly with each midwife, an appropriate follow-up and communication plan based on identified needs.
●
Provide follow-up counselling and psychosocial support through telephone or in-person, as appropriate.
●
Maintain regular and appropriate contact with midwives requiring continued psychosocial support.
●
Monitor progress and adjust the frequency and type of support according to individual needs.
3. Referral and Case Management
●
Identify individuals who may require specialized mental health or other professional services beyond the scope of the counselling provided.
●
Facilitate appropriate and confidential referrals to available specialized services in accordance with established referral pathways.
●
Follow up on referrals, where appropriate and with the individual's consent, while respecting confidentiality and professional boundaries.
4. Staff Welfare and Capacity Support
●
Contribute to the overall staff welfare approach for midwives working in targeted facilities.
●
Identify common psychosocial stressors and emerging staff welfare concerns affecting midwives.
●
Where appropriate, provide brief group-based psychosocial support, stress-management, or well-being sessions for midwives.
●
Provide practical recommendations on measures that may contribute to improved staff well-being and retention.
5. Coordination and Reporting
●
Coordinate closely with the supervisor and designated focal point of the implementing partner.
●
Maintain appropriate documentation of counselling and psychosocial support activities while ensuring strict confidentiality.
●
Provide regular anonymized reports on counselling activities, psychosocial needs, key challenges, referrals, and recommendations to strengthen staff welfare and support.
●
Immediately communicate any significant operational or service-delivery concerns through the appropriate reporting channels, while maintaining client confidentiality.
●
Participate in relevant coordination, review, and planning meetings as requested.
Approach and Modality:
The assignment will follow a blended model of MHPSS support, combining face-to-face and remote counselling. The MHPSS Senior Counsellor will initially visit the targeted FHHs and MLMCCs to establish contact with midwives, conduct an initial psychosocial assessment, and provide counselling/support. Following the initial visit, the counsellor will develop an individualized follow-up plan with each midwife. Subsequent support may be provided through telephone-based counselling and psychosocial check-ins, particularly for midwives working in remote locations. The frequency of follow-up will be determined according to the individual midwife's needs and the agreed communication plan. The MHPSS counsellor is expected to ensure that the modality of support is accessible, confidential, culturally appropriate, and consistent with professional ethical standards.

Title: Medical Doctor Team Leader
Education: Advanced university degree in medicine or other paramedical studies,Desirable degree in Public Health. [DESIRABLE]

About Company:
Over the past few years, Afghanistan has witnessed a relative improvement in security and stability across much of the country. This has allowed humanitarian actors like INTERSOS to maintain uninterrupted access and expand services in areas that were previously hard to reach. Despite this progress, the humanitarian situation remains critical, with millions of Afghans continuing to face acute vulnerabilities due to prolonged economic hardship, natural disasters, and limited access to essential services.
In 2025, more than half of the population is in need of humanitarian assistance, with food insecurity, child malnutrition, and displacement remaining key concerns. Natural disasters, such as floods and recent earthquakes, have further compounded the needs of already struggling communities.
INTERSOS continues to operate through a community-based approach with field bases in Kabul, Kandahar, and Zabul, delivering primary healthcare, nutrition, and protection services with a focus on women, children, and persons with disabilities. The organization enjoys strong community acceptance and collaborates closely with relevant national authorities, including maintaining the full participation of female staff in all activities.
While the operational environment is largely stable and conducive, funding shortfalls and systemic barriers such as restrictions on financial flows and administrative bottlenecks continue to impact the scope and scale of humanitarian response. Sustained support is crucial to ensure the continuity of life-saving services and to address the urgent needs of Afghanistan’s most vulnerable populations.

To lead and manage the health/nutrition team and contribute to a reduced maternal and children morbidity and mortality associated with malnutrition, vaccine preventable, communicable, common childhood illnesses, reproductive health, and hazards resulting from deficient (or non-existing) health and nutrition services, environmental health conditions and protection environment in conflict-affected communities.

Job Summary:
Position Purpose
The Provincial
HIVA Focal Point
provides provincial leadership for the coordinated implementation, quality assurance, monitoring and reporting of HIVA project interventions in
Badghis
. The postholder serves as the primary link between supported health facilities, provincial stakeholders and the Kabul programme team, ensuring that activities are delivered on time, evidence is reliable, clinical mentorship is followed through, resources are used responsibly, and services comply with applicable national protocols, donor requirements and ARDHO standards.
Expected Contribution
·
Translate the approved work plan into coordinated provincial implementation across supported facilities.
·
Strengthen the quality and continuity of maternal, newborn and other HIVA-supported health services through supervision, coaching and corrective follow-up.
·
Maintain credible programme evidence through accurate data verification, timely reporting and complete documentation.
·
Anticipate operational, supply, safeguarding and security risks and escalate critical issues early.
Key Accountabilities and Responsibilities
1. Provincial Project Leadership and Coordination
·
Develop and maintain a detailed provincial activity schedule derived from the approved project work plan, including targets, responsible persons, dependencies and reporting deadlines.
·
Coordinate and oversee implementation across assigned health facilities, ensuring consistency with project objectives, approved budgets, technical guidance and donor commitments.
·
Track daily and weekly implementation status; identify delays, bottlenecks or deviations; agree corrective actions; and escalate issues requiring central-level decisions.
·
Maintain structured communication with facility teams, clinical mentors and the Kabul office so decisions, risks and operational changes are communicated promptly.
·
Convene or participate in provincial coordination meetings, field reviews and implementation sessions; document decisions, owners and deadlines and follow through to closure.
·
Support integration of HIVA interventions within existing health services to strengthen continuity, efficiency, local ownership and sustainability.
·
Ensure activities are delivered in a culturally appropriate, gender-responsive and community-oriented manner that promotes access, dignity and acceptance.
2. Stakeholder Engagement and Representation
·
Serve as ARDHO’s designated provincial contact for day-to-day HIVA project coordination within the limits of delegated authority.
·
Maintain professional working relationships with Provincial Public Health Directorate representatives, health-facility leadership, community structures, implementing partners and other relevant stakeholders.
·
Communicate project scope, implementation status, challenges and agreed actions accurately and consistently, without making commitments beyond approved authority.
·
Represent ARDHO in authorized meetings and technical forums; prepare briefing points in advance and submit concise meeting records and follow-up actions.
·
Promote community feedback and accountability, ensuring significant concerns are recorded, referred and followed through under ARDHO procedures.
3. Monitoring, Data Quality and Reporting
·
Maintain a provincial monitoring calendar covering facility visits, mentorship follow-up, data-verification activities, report deadlines and review meetings.
·
Collect, review and validate routine programme data from supported facilities, checking completeness, internal consistency, source-document alignment and unusual variances before submission.
·
Work with facility teams to correct data-quality gaps and strengthen registers, reporting tools, filing systems and evidence retention.
·
Prepare accurate, analytical and timely weekly and monthly progress reports that compare results against targets, explain variances, identify risks and recommend management action.
·
Support preparation of quarterly and annual summaries, mentorship-visit schedules, presentation materials, success examples and other programme documentation as requested.
·
Maintain an organized electronic and hard-copy filing system for plans, reports, attendance records, supervision tools, action plans, meeting minutes and approved correspondence.
·
Protect patient, staff and project information, applying confidentiality and authorized information-sharing requirements at all times.
4. Clinical Quality Assurance and Supportive Supervision
·
Conduct regular supportive-supervision visits using approved tools to assess service quality, protocol adherence, staff performance, documentation and patient-centred care.
·
Verify compliance with Ministry of Public Health guidance, relevant national standards, HIVA technical requirements and ARDHO quality benchmarks.
·
Document service-delivery gaps, analyse likely causes and agree practical corrective action plans with clear owners, deadlines and verification methods.
·
Monitor completion and effectiveness of corrective actions and escalate recurring or high-risk deficiencies to technical and programme leadership.
·
Conduct post-mentorship follow-up with facilities visited by clinical mentors and document whether agreed practice improvements are being applied.
·
Provide clinical mentors with current information on maternal and newborn health and HII initiatives as defined in project technical guidance, and coordinate required follow-up.
5. Capacity Development and Mentorship
·
Assess learning needs through supervision findings, data reviews, staff consultation and observed performance gaps.
·
Support the design, scheduling and delivery of competency-focused training, orientation, refresher sessions and on-the-job coaching for relevant health-facility personnel.
·
Provide respectful, practical and evidence-based mentorship to clinicians, nurses, midwives, community health workers and other assigned personnel within the postholder’s professional competence.
·
Participate as trainer, co-facilitator or trainee in authorized provincial and central training events and complete all required training documentation.
·
Promote peer learning, case review and dissemination of approved good practices across supported facilities.
·
Evaluate whether training has changed knowledge, practice or service quality and recommend additional support where improvement is not sustained.
6. Medicines, Supplies and Resource Stewardship
·
Monitor the availability, condition, storage and appropriate use of essential medicines, medical supplies, equipment and project materials at supported facilities.
·
Review stock records and consumption patterns, identify potential shortages, expiry risks, overstocking or unusual usage and report them through the appropriate channel.
·
Support realistic forecasting and timely requests based on service trends, planned activities and verified facility needs.
·
Coordinate with logistics and supply-chain colleagues regarding approved procurement, delivery, distribution and receipt of commodities.
·
Verify that facility-level records support accountability and traceability and that project resources are used only for authorized purposes.
·
Promptly report stock-outs, losses, damage, suspected diversion or other material control concerns.
7. Risk, Safety, Safeguarding and Compliance
·
Maintain a provincial risk and issue log covering operational, technical, supply, financial, access, safety, security and reputational risks.
·
Monitor changing field conditions and early-warning indicators; recommend proportionate mitigation and contingency measures to protect service continuity.
·
Immediately report critical incidents, serious service-quality concerns, safeguarding allegations, fraud indicators and significant security developments through approved channels.
·
Comply with and promote ARDHO policies on PSEAH, child safeguarding, code of conduct, confidentiality, anti-fraud, health and safety and grievance response.
·
Ensure field activities apply do-no-harm, non-discrimination, informed participation and respect for patient dignity and privacy.
·
Support implementation of approved contingency plans and document lessons after disruptions or significant incidents.

Title: Regional Team Coordinator (Re Announced)
Salary: Salary and conditions are according to ACBAR’s salary scale.
Contract Duration: Contract is through 31 December, 2026, renewable on an annual basis depending on funding and performance.
Education: Bachelor’s Degree in a relevant field, including but not limited to Project Management, Humanitarian Aid, Development Policy, Business and/or Management, or another specialized field relevant to the role.  Master’s Degree is preferred.
Experience: Minimum seven (7) years of professional experience working with either NGOs or the UN in Afghanistan managing or leading humanitarian and/or development programs at the field level.
About Company:
The Agency Coordinating Body for Afghan Relief and Development (ACBAR) is an independent forum founded in 1988 in response to the demand from NGOs working with Afghan refugees in Pakistan and across the border in Afghanistan to more efficiently coordinate assistance and delivery of services. With its main office in Kabul since 2002, ACBAR brings together more than 200 National and International NGOs working in all sectors of humanitarian assistance and development in Afghanistan. Based on our three strategic pillars of Information and Coordination, Advocacy and Enabling Environment, and Capacity Building, ACBAR’s activities support our members to effectively deliver services and implement programs across Afghanistan, as well as provide services that promote ongoing organizational development and learning.   ACBAR is committed to providing
an efficient platform for members to carry out effective humanitarian, development, and peace building activities in Afghanistan.
The members are the drive behind ACBAR, and their active participation is essential to ACBAR’s continued dynamism.
With the ongoing humanitarian reset, ACBAR is taking a stronger role providing programmatic coordination for our members and implementing NGOs in numerous areas, including sub-national coordination. This year, ACBAR will serve in the secretariat role supporting newly operationalized Regional Teams (RT) in five regional hubs (Kandahar, Herat, Nangarhar, Balkh and Bamiyan).  These RTs will be responsible to support Area Based Coordination and nexus-oriented approaches in their respective regions, and responsible for coordinating BHN activities and supporting the transition from humanitarian to BHN programming where feasible and appropriate.
Job Summary:
POSITION SUMMARY
The Regional Team Coordinator (RT) supports ACBAR’s role as Secretariat to the Regional Teams (RTs), which serve as the primary sub-national coordination platform under Afghanistan’s Area-Based Coordination (ABC) and Humanitarian-Development-Peace Nexus (HDPN) framework. The RT Coordinator will ensure effective, inclusive, and well-documented coordination among Humanitarian and Basic Human Needs (BHN) actors, facilitating evidence-based planning, information sharing, and follow-up on priorities of the RT, in cooperation with two RT co-chairs per region. As part of the ACBAR team, the RT Coordinator will also engage with ACBAR’s full regional team to support the central role that ACBAR plays to strengthen NGO engagement, supporting transition from humanitarian to resilience-oriented programming, and ensuring alignment with national coordination structures.
ESSENTIAL TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES FOR THE POSITION
Secretariat and Coordination Leadership
Serve as the primary focal point for secretariat functions of the Regional Team (RT), which will be responsible to organize and coordinate monthly (and ad hoc) RT meetings, including developing priorities and agendas for meetings in consultation with RT co-chairs.
Draft and circulate meeting minutes of the RT meetings to co-chairs and all participants for further follow up on key discussions
,
decisions taken, and action points and engagement with responsible parties
Maintain updated RT membership lists and track regular participation by RT members to ensure robust engagement, facilitating inclusive participation of members, including remote/online engagement as required.
Track follow-up actions and monitor implementation of RT decisions, being the key point person to ensure that decisions taken by the RT are operationalized.
Manage integration of various other coordination platforms into the work of the RT, including the OCT (humanitarian coordination), national coordination structures (ICCT, HCT, PMT)
,
and NGO forums.
This will include actively identifying and resolving duplication, gaps or inconsistencies, and ensuring alignment with national priorities.
External Engagement and Access Support
Serve as the main focal point for external engagement on behalf of the RT, including direct engagement with provincial and local authorities, community leaders and other stakeholders required to support an enabling environment for implementing humanitarian and basic needs programs.  While leading external engagement, the RT Coordinator will engage with the co-chairs, NGOs and UN partners to successfully facilitate the engagement on behalf of the RT.
Escalate and report ongoing access and implementation challenges to the national level management of ACBAR, HAWG, and corresponding coordination mechanisms.
Strategy, Planning and Information Management
Lead the development of the RT annual action plan in cooperation with the co-chairs and members, with clear objectives and deliverables that can be tracked and monitored to demonstrate the contributions and value-add of the RT to members.
Lead information management and communication for the RT, including distribution of monthly summaries of activities to members, maintaining regular communication with co-chairs and members to carry forward RT priorities and strategies, and provide regional briefings to national coordination platforms, as needed.
Support regional-based data collection, assessments, and analysis to inform both regional and national level strategic planning, including providing support to data collection for the Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan (HNRP) and the UN Strategic Framework for Afghanistan (UNSFA) and other analytic and research-oriented products and reports at the regional and national level. This will include data collection related to coordination of activities, including support for maintain an accurate 3W’s.
Support preparation of reports, updates, presentations, etc. on the ongoing work of the RT for HCT, UNCT, ACBAR Steering Committee, Donors and other interested external stakeholders.
Durable Solutions, Nexus Integration and Early Response Coordination
Support leadership of a Durable Solutions Technical Sub-Group of the RT that will support priorities of BHN programs within the region and provide support in transitioning from humanitarian to early recovery strategies.
Support coordination between the RT, ACBAR and the OCT in the event of rapid onset emergencies to streamline activities of the RT and emergency response coordination, and to ensure planning for transition from immediate response to early recovery priorities.  This will include facilitating rapid information sharing, initial situational overview, and regular coordination between all actors, in alignment with OCT coordination.
Cross-Cutting Priorities
Support strategic initiatives to promote better community engagement, accountability to affected populations (AAP), support for disability inclusion, and principled programming.
Ensure integration of key cross-cutting issues in RT coordination, including protection and centrality of protection, equality, GBV risk mitigation, PSEA reporting, and conflict sensitivity and Do No Harm principles.
Support strategic initiatives to promote Localisation, including facilitation of strong presence, participation and leadership of national and local NGOs, CSOs and WLOs within the work of the RT.
Engage with and support the ongoing work of the ACBAR Regional Office to ensure alignment with ACBAR strategic priorities and the ongoing work of the RT.
Job Requirements:
EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE REQUIREMENTS:
Bachelor’s Degree in a relevant field, including but not limited to Project Management, Humanitarian Aid, Development Policy, Business and/or Management, or another specialized field relevant to the role.  Master’s Degree is preferred.
Minimum seven (7) years of professional experience working with either NGOs or the UN in Afghanistan managing or leading humanitarian and/or development programs at the field level.
Minimum three (3) years of experience supporting NGOs or UN in humanitarian coordination and representation roles.
Preference given to candidates who have worked in numerous locations in Afghanistan, including direct field work.
OTHER DESIRED SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE AND ATTRIBUTES:
Previous experience managing small-to-medium sized teams and working with many different stakeholder groups, including international organizations.
Strong analytical skills, with the ability to develop strategies and technical reports in English, Dari and/or Pashto.
Experience representing an NGO or UN agency with varied external stakeholders, including provincial and regional government officials.
Ability to manage complex coordination environments, with the ability operate under pressure and ambiguity.
Strong facilitation and negotiation skills.
The ability to work with other in a respectful and professional manner and work well as the leader of a team.

Job Summary:
Position Summary
The Chief Surveyor is responsible for managing and supervising all surveying and setting-out activities for a road construction project. The role ensures that the road alignment, levels, coordinates, earthworks, structures, drainage, and other works are constructed accurately in accordance with approved drawings, specifications, and contractual requirements.
Job Requirements:
Job Description — Chief Surveyor, Road Project
Key Responsibilities
Manage and supervise the surveying team, including surveyors, technicians, and chainmen.
Establish and maintain project control points, benchmarks, reference stations, and survey networks.
Carry out and verify setting-out for:
Road centerline and alignment
Horizontal and vertical curves
Formation and subgrade levels
Embankments and cuttings
Pavement layers
Drainage structures and culverts
Bridges and other structures
Road furniture and ancillary works
Check coordinates, elevations, chainages, offsets, and dimensions against approved drawings.
Conduct topographical, longitudinal, and cross-sectional surveys as required.
Monitor earthwork quantities and assist with measurement and quantity calculations.
Carry out as-built surveys and prepare accurate survey records and drawings.
Review survey data and ensure accuracy before submitting it for approval.
Coordinate with the Project Manager, Construction Manager, Site Engineers, QA/QC team, and consultant's survey team.
Review construction drawings and identify discrepancies or conflicts affecting setting-out.
Ensure that surveying activities comply with project specifications, method statements, quality requirements, and applicable standards.
Operate and oversee the use of total stations, GNSS/GPS equipment, digital levels, drones where approved, and relevant surveying software.
Ensure all surveying equipment is properly maintained, calibrated, and in good working condition.
Maintain survey field books, control-point registers, calibration records, level books, calculation sheets, and other survey documentation.
Verify contractor/subcontractor survey work where applicable.
Assist the quantity surveying and commercial teams with measurement and verification of completed works.
Provide technical guidance and training to junior surveyors and survey technicians.
Identify and resolve survey-related technical issues during construction.
Ensure safe working practices are followed during all surveying activities.
Required Qualifications
Bachelor's degree or diploma in Surveying, Geomatics, Civil Engineering, or a related discipline.
Professional surveying certification or registration is an advantage.
Strong knowledge of land surveying principles and road construction surveying.
Good knowledge of coordinate systems, benchmarks, levels, alignment, and setting-out procedures.
Proficiency with Total Station, GNSS/GPS, AutoCAD/Civil 3D, digital levels, and relevant surveying software.
Experience
Typically 9–12+ years of surveying experience, preferably with significant experience on major road/highway projects.
Previous experience in a Chief Surveyor or Senior Surveyor position is preferred.
Experience in earthworks, pavement construction, drainage, bridges, and road structures.
Experience working with consultants, contractors, and government/road authorities is an advantage.
Key Competencies
Strong technical surveying and analytical skills.
Excellent knowledge of road construction methods and tolerances.
High attention to accuracy and detail.
Ability to read and interpret engineering drawings and specifications.
Strong leadership and team-management skills.
Good communication and coordination abilities.
Ability to work under pressure and meet construction deadlines.
Strong problem-solving and decision-making skills.
Commitment to quality, safety, and accurate documentation.
Reporting
The Chief Surveyor typically reports to the Project Manager / Construction Manager and coordinates closely with the Consultant/Engineer, QA/QC Manager, Site Engineers, and Quantity Surveyor.

Job Summary:
How can you make a difference?
In Afghanistan, UNICEF operates in a complex and evolving context, characterized by protracted humanitarian needs, deep-rooted structural vulnerabilities, and limited access to basic services. The Country Office implements a dual programming approach that combines humanitarian action and basic human needs (BHN) programming, supporting life-saving interventions while contributing to longer-term resilience and development outcomes.
UNICEF’s engagement is grounded in the Core Commitments for Children in Humanitarian Action (CCCs) and guided by the principles of neutrality, impartiality, and independence. The office actively contributes to inter-agency coordination platforms, including sector and cluster coordination groups for Nutrition, WASH, Education, and Child Protection. It also supports the Afghanistan community and humanitarian partners in improving service delivery, evidence-based planning, and accountability.
Information management plays a central role in enabling UNICEF to fulfil its programmatic commitments and coordination responsibilities. In Afghanistan, a robust IM function is essential to ensure the integration of humanitarian and BHN indicators, systematic tracking of AWP and CPD results, and effective monitoring of convergence districts prioritized for multi-sectoral action. IM also underpins UNICEF’s ability to contribute to key reports such as the Humanitarian Response Plan (HRP), UNSFA, Situation Reports (SitReps), and the Results Assessment Module (RAM), and to strengthen partner accountability and decision-making at all levels.
Job organizational context:

Ensure proper documentation and quality control of IHC procedures.

Perform internal quality control and troubleshoot instrument problems.

Maintain confidentiality of patient information and laboratory results.

Follow laboratory biosafety and infection-control procedures.
Properly use PPE and handle biological specimens safely.
Dispose of sharps, chemicals, and biological waste according to laboratory policies.
Follow procedures for spills, exposure incidents, and other laboratory emergencies.

Job Summary:
The Chief Risk Officer (CRO) should report and have direct access to the Board of Supervisors or its risk committee without impediment.
The CRO should have the ability to interpret and articulate risk in a clear and understandable manner and to effectively engage the board and management in constructive dialogue on key risk issues. Interaction between the CRO and the board and/or risk committee should occur regularly, and the CRO should have the ability to meet with the board or risk committee without executive directors being present.
Risks should be identified, monitored and controlled on an ongoing bank-wide and individual entity basis. The sophistication of the bank’s risk management and internal control infrastructure should keep pace with changes to the bank’s risk profile, to the external risk landscape and in industry practice
.
Risk identification should encompass all material risks to the bank, on- and off-balance sheet and on a group-wide, portfolio-wise and business-line level. In order to perform effective risk assessments, the Board and senior management, including the CRO, should, regularly and on an ad hoc basis, evaluate the risks faced by the bank and its overall risk profile. The risk assessment process should include ongoing analysis of existing risks as well as the identification of new or emerging risks. Risks should be captured from all organizational units. Concentrations associated with material risks should likewise be factored into the risk assessment.
Risk identification and measurement should include both quantitative and qualitative elements. Risk measurements should also include qualitative, bank-wide views of risk relative to the bank’s external operating environment. Banks should also consider and evaluate harder-to-quantify risks, such as reputation risk.
Information should be communicated to the Board of Supervisors and Board of Management in a timely, accurate and understandable manner so that they are equipped to take informed decisions. While ensuring that Board of Supervisors and Board of Management are sufficiently informed, management and those responsible for the risk management function should avoid voluminous information that can make it difficult to identify key issues. Rather, information should be prioritized and presented in a concise, fully contextualized manner. The board should assess the relevance and the process for maintaining the accuracy of the information it receives and determine if additional or less information is needed.
Risk reporting systems should be dynamic, comprehensive and accurate, and should draw on a range of underlying assumptions.
Banks should avoid organizational “silos” that can impede effective sharing of information across an organization and can result in decisions being taken in isolation from the rest of the bank. Overcoming these information-sharing obstacles may require the Board of Supervisors, Board of Management and control functions to re-evaluate established practices in order to encourage greater communication.

Propose policy implications for risk management to the BOS based on laws, regulations, and internationally accepted standards.
Draft, amend, improve, and propose policies and procedures for risk management.
Pursue the risk management objectives in line with the policies & procedures, and size & complexity of the bank business.
Risk Measurement Tools
Develop and improve internal rating system for measuring risks associated with fund-based and non-fund-based exposures.
Develop risk grading metrics for country risk and correspondent institutions risk.
Develop monitoring tools for various risks in accordance with internationally accepted norms and practices.
Regulatory Framework & Limits
Setting prudential limits and thresholds based on risk appetite of the bank in the policy documents.
Tracking and monitoring the state of adherence to prudential limits and thresholds stipulated in the internal policies of the bank.
Study on applicability of the international norms and best practices to align the practice in the local context of Afghanistan.
Credit Risk
Study of exposures in respect to single party/large exposure against regulatory and policy benchmarks,
Study of credit concentration with respect to sector, geography, and products,
Periodic analysis of distressed assets and reporting to the BOS.

Develop liquidity risk monitoring and reporting tools,
Review & study of country risk exposures against limits set, including positions of NOSTRO and correspondent banks.
Review & monitoring of open forex position and currency concentration.

Strong knowledge and experience of operational risk and its measurement
Regular review and monitoring operational risk in all branches of the bank,
Periodic reporting of operational events to BOS and develop tools for risk identification, management, and reporting.

Periodic risk assessment of departments to ensure a transparent and efficient governance of the bank, including efficiency of policies, procedures, workforce capacity, and so on,

Job Summary:
Job brief:
Prepares proposals by determining concept; gathering and formatting information; writing drafts; obtaining approvals. The proposal writer works in many different industries to create clear, succinct documents that suggest a course of action or idea. The proposal writer is expected to write well-- grammar, spelling and context all count. His/ her key asset would be the ability to write under tight deadlines, be organized and prepared, and have the ability to say much with a few words.
Responsibilities:
Best relation with donors and seeker new donor.
Excellent communications skills with donors to get proposal approval with donor satisfaction.
Determines proposal concept by identifying and clarifying opportunities and needs; studying requests for proposal (RFPs); attending strategy meetings.
Meets proposal deadline by establishing priorities and target dates for information gathering, writing, review, and approval; entering and monitoring tracking data; coordinating requirements with contributors; contributing proposal status information to review meetings; transmitting proposals.
Gathers proposal information by identifying sources of information; coordinating submissions and collections; identifying and communicating risks associated with proposals.
Develops proposal by assembling information including project nature, objectives/outcomes/deliverables, implementation, methods, timetable, staffing, budget, standards of performance, and evaluation; writing, revising, and editing drafts including executive summaries, conclusions, and organization credentials.
Prepares presentation by evaluating text, graphics, and binding; coordinating printing.
Maintains quality results by using templates; following proposal-writing standards including readability, consistency, and tone; maintaining proposal support databases.
Obtains approvals by reviewing proposal with key providers and project managers.
Improves proposal-writing results by evaluating and re-designing processes, approach, coordination, and boilerplate; implementing changes.
Updates job knowledge by participating in educational opportunities; maintaining personal networks.
Accomplishes company goals by accepting ownership for accomplishing new and different requests; exploring opportunities to add value to job accomplishments.

Interested and qualified national candidates should submit a cover letter explaining their motivation and updated CV to the following email address:  hr.erto.worldwide@gmail.com job title is very importent in subject line.
The closing date for accepting applications is open.

Note: The applications received after the closing date will not be considered and only short-listed candidates will be called for an interview.
Due to the urgent need of the role, the interview may take place before the closing date of the post.
